# idsec_pamsh_account (Resource)

Manage Privilege Cloud account information, metadata, and credentials
<!-- BEGIN CUSTOM NOTES -->
<!-- END CUSTOM NOTES -->

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `safe_name` (String) The Safe where the account will be created

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `address` (String) The name or address of the machine where the account will be used
- `name` (String) Name of the account
- `platform_account_properties` (Dynamic) The object containing key-value pairs to associate with the account, as defined by the account platform. Optional properties that do not exist or internal properties are not returned
- `platform_id` (String) The platform assigned to this account
- `secret` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The secret value. Write-only: this value is never stored in Terraform state or plan. It is sent to the API on create, and on update whenever it changes; rotation is detected automatically via the computed `secret_write_only_hash` attribute, so no manual trigger needs to be bumped. Requires Terraform 1.11 or later.

<!-- BEGIN ATTR NOTE: secret -->
~> The secret attribute has been migrated to a hashed write-only attribute, which means that any value will not be stored in the state file in plain text i.e., it will be null, even if set in the configuration. Any outputs and locals that reference the state value of secret e.g., `idsec_pamsh_account.example_resource.secret` will be null as well.After `terraform import` you will notice an update on subsequent `terrafrom apply` e.g.: `+ secret_write_only_hash = (sensitive value)`. The value configured at import time is recorded into Terraform state without being written to the vault. Because state then matches your configuration, no later apply will write it either, even though the vault still holds the old credential. To actually set the credential, change `secret` to a different value on a subsequent apply.
<!-- END ATTR NOTE: secret -->
- `secret_management` (Attributes) Secret management configuration for the account (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--secret_management))
- `secret_type` (String) The type of secret for the acccount (password,key)
- `user_name` (String) The account username
- `username` (String) Account user's name

### Read-Only

- `category_modification_time` (Number) The last time the account or one of its file categories was created or changed
- `created_time` (Number) The date and time the account was created
- `id` (String) The unique ID of the account to updatee
- `secret_write_only_hash` (String, Sensitive) Automatically computed hash of secret. Changes when the secret changes; used to detect rotation without storing the raw value in state.
- `status` (String) The account's management status
